claims.claim: Ravfogel, Goldberg and Goldberger find that the probability of the correct next word actually falling inside an OPT model's top-p set is lower than p, so the models are overconfident and the nucleus does not carry its stated probabilistic meaning.
claims.source: Ravfogel, Goldberg, Goldberger, 'Conformal Nucleus Sampling', arXiv:2305.02633v1 (2023); Findings of ACL 2023
claims.quote: that OPT models are overconfident, and that
claims.modelEra: OPT models from 125M to 30B parameters, observation May 2023; register measured: 10,000 English Wikipedia sentences plus OpenWebText prefixes

claims.claim: Ravfogel and colleagues report that the model's overconfidence is worst in its lowest-entropy contexts, the moments where a truncation sampler narrows the candidate set hardest.
claims.source: Ravfogel, Goldberg, Goldberger, arXiv:2305.02633v1 (2023); Findings of ACL 2023
claims.quote: when the model is apparently the most
claims.page: Section 3, per-entropy calibration results (ten entropy bins)
claims.modelEra: OPT 125M to 30B, May 2023; register measured: English Wikipedia

claims.claim: Ravfogel and colleagues report that calibration of the top-p set shows a moderate inverse scaling with model size, so the larger OPT models were not better calibrated.
claims.source: Ravfogel, Goldberg, Goldberger, arXiv:2305.02633v1 (2023); Findings of ACL 2023
claims.quote: calibration shows a moderate inverse scaling
claims.modelEra: OPT 125M, 350M, 1.3B, 13B and 30B, May 2023; register measured: English Wikipedia

claims.claim: Ravfogel and colleagues measured calibration on ten thousand English Wikipedia items, one of the few decoding studies to work in the encyclopedic register.
claims.source: Ravfogel, Goldberg, Goldberger, arXiv:2305.02633v1 (2023); Findings of ACL 2023
claims.quote: We ran the models on 10,000 English Wikipedia
claims.modelEra: OPT family, May 2023; register measured: English Wikipedia

claims.claim: Borec, Sadler and Schlangen report that widening the nucleus reduces verbatim memorisation only modestly in two fine-tuned GPT-Neo models.
claims.source: Borec, Sadler, Schlangen, 'The Unreasonable Ineffectiveness of Nucleus Sampling on Mitigating Text Memorization', arXiv:2408.16345v1 (2024)
claims.quote: of the nucleus size reduces memorization only
claims.modelEra: two GPT-Neo models fine-tuned on a diagnostic duplicate corpus, August 2024; register measured: a constructed duplicate-controlled dataset

claims.claim: Borec, Sadler and Schlangen name a soft memorisation in which a model's output echoes its training data without reproducing it word for word, and which survives nucleus sampling.
